title: Chromosomes, Genes & DNA
description: The instructions that make you 'you' are hidden in the nucleus. Decode chromosomes and genes to grab piece 5's core.

content.value: Inside the nucleus are thread-like structures called CHROMOSOMES. They carry the instructions for building and running the whole organism, and for passing features from parents to their children.

Chromosomes are made up of smaller units called GENES. A gene is a unit of HEREDITY — it decides features such as eye colour, hair type, and height, and passes them from parents to offspring. This is why you resemble your family.

NUCLEUS
 └── CHROMOSOMES (thread-like carriers)
       └── GENES (units of heredity)
             └── made of DNA (the instruction molecule)

Genes are made of a molecule called DNA. DNA carries coded instructions, a bit like a recipe book, that tell the cell how to build and run the organism. Every cell in your body carries a copy of these instructions in its nucleus.
Think of it as nested boxes: the nucleus holds chromosomes, chromosomes contain genes, and genes are made of DNA. Genes are why children resemble their parents.
Key Takeaway: The nucleus contains chromosomes, which are made of genes. Genes are the units of heredity (made of DNA) that carry features from parents to offspring.
